u23: This firmware (0.1.0) has been bench-tested on a custom ESP32-C3 board wired to a Betaflight flight controller and a GoPro HERO11 Black. It has not been flight tested, and some camera protocol values are still being verified against live captures. Treat every flight as a test flight. Do all setup and testing on the bench with propellers removed, and check every behaviour in this guide before you fly with it.
u25: RecLink only reads from your flight controller and writes OSD text. It cannot arm, disarm, move motors, change PIDs or touch the radio link. That boundary is enforced in the firmware itself, not left to convention. If RecLink fails, the worst thing that can happen in flight is that the OSD text stops updating.
u27: Chapters 1–6 take you from a bare board to a paired camera and are meant to be followed in order. Chapters 7–12 explain each part of the web configurator. Chapters 13 and 14 cover day-to-day use and what to do when something is wrong. Screenshots show the real configurator on a phone.
u37: A small ESP32 board that sits between your flight controller and your action camera, so the camera is controlled by the aircraft and reports back on your OSD.
u57: RecLink listens to the flight controller over a three-wire serial link and talks to the camera over Bluetooth. The Wi-Fi network exists only while the aircraft is disarmed, for configuration.
u59: Camera info on the OSD. Recording state, elapsed and remaining time, camera battery, SD space, resolution, frame rate and link status, as 22 tokens across four 16-character lines you design yourself.
u60: Recording that follows the aircraft. Start and stop on arm, on a radio switch, or on a combination. Every command is checked against what the camera reports.
u61: Camera settings from a switch. A 2–6 position switch or knob selects zones. On a GoPro each zone pushes its own resolution, frame rate, lens, HyperSmooth and Protune values. On a DJI each zone selects a camera mode.
u62: Highlight tags from a momentary switch (GoPro HiLight, DJI Quick-Switch).
u63: Up to four paired cameras, any mix of GoPro and DJI. At power-up it connects to the strongest one in range.
u64: Clock sync from the flight controller's GPS time, so footage carries the right timestamp.
u65: One web page for all configuration, plus firmware updates. No app, no cloud.
u68: Never sends RC, GPS, clock, display or reboot commands to the flight controller, and never changes its configuration.
u69: Never arms or disarms the aircraft.
u70: Never runs Wi-Fi while armed. The access point is shut down within 100 ms of arming.
u71: Never powers the camera, and never formats a card or deletes files from automation.
u72: Never shows a value the camera has not confirmed. An unknown value renders blank, not 0 and not a guess.
u77: Betaflight 2025.12.0 or newer (MSP API 1.47+). Older versions cannot show custom OSD messages.
u80: HERO 11, 12, 13, and newer models that use the same Open GoPro Bluetooth API
u84: Analog and digital. Digital mode limits output to the glyphs DJI-style goggles can draw.
u88: A RecLink board, a free UART on your flight controller, and a camera that is on its own power.

u134: Serial wires cross: the FC's TX goes to RecLink's RX, and RecLink's TX goes to the FC's RX.
u135: Pick a free UART on the flight controller and note its number. You will enable MSP on that UART in chapter 4.
u136: Connect the four wires as drawn. The board's TX line has a 470 Ω series resistor on the board. Do not add another.
u137: Add the capacitor if needed. Bluetooth and Wi-Fi transmit bursts draw about 350 mA peaks. On a long thin harness this can pull the supply down and reset the board. A 220 µF or larger low-ESR capacitor across the 5 V pads prevents that.
u138: Mount it close to the camera. Keep the board's antenna clear of carbon fibre and battery leads. Bluetooth range to the camera is the part that suffers from bad placement.
u139: Leave the camera's power alone. The camera runs from its own battery or BEC. RecLink never powers or biases it.
u140: Crossed the wires? No need to resolder
u141: If TX and RX end up swapped on a four-pin harness, you can fix it in the configurator: Network → Swap TX/RX pins (advanced mode), then reboot. See chapter 12.
u143: The board takes 5 V from the flight controller through its onboard regulator. Check that the pad you use is 5 V and not battery voltage before you connect. The board has a brown-out detector: a dip in supply resets it and it recovers on its own within about 300 ms, but the OSD text freezes for that moment.
u146: Two changes in Betaflight Configurator: turn on MSP on the UART you wired, and make four custom message elements visible on the OSD.
u148: Custom OSD messages exist only in Betaflight 2025.12.0 and newer (MSP API 1.47 or higher). They were not added to older versions. If your firmware is older, update it first. RecLink reports "FC too old for custom OSD" if it detects an older API.
u150: Connect the flight controller to Betaflight Configurator over USB and open the Ports tab.
u151: On the row for the UART you wired, switch on MSP in the Configuration/MSP column. Leave the baud rate at 115200.
u153: Menu names can shift slightly between Configurator versions. The setting you need is "MSP on that UART at 115200 baud". If you must use another speed, set the same value in RecLink under Network → Baud rate (advanced mode) and reboot it.
u154: 2. Show the four custom message elements
u156: In the element list, tick Custom message 1, 2, 3 and 4 (until RecLink writes to them, Betaflight displays their placeholder names). Switch them on in the profile you fly.
u157: Drag each of the four into the layout. Each one is an independent element: put them where your goggles have room. A neat column in the left or right third works well.
u158: Save. Keep every line within 16 characters; that is the most Betaflight allows per message.
u166: You only need to place the elements once. RecLink changes their text; Betaflight keeps the position. Keep them away from where you read battery voltage and warnings.
u168: Pick your OSD type in the configurator's OSD tab. Digital (the default) is safe for DJI-style goggles; analog allows the full character set. See chapter 10.
u170: RecLink reads the transmitter's channels through the flight controller. If you want a switch to start recording or select zones, assign it to a free AUX channel in your radio and confirm in Betaflight's Receiver tab that the bar moves. RecLink counts channels the same way Betaflight does: AUX 1 is channel 5. You do not need a Betaflight mode for these switches. In chapter 8 you will find the right channel by flipping the switch and letting RecLink detect it.
u172: First power-up and the web configurator
u173: Power the quad, join RecLink's Wi-Fi from your phone, and open the configurator. Everything from here on is done in that page.
u175: Remove the propellers, then power the flight controller from a battery or USB. The RecLink LED lights solid while it boots.
u176: Wait for the portal. When the board sees the flight controller and the aircraft is disarmed, it starts its own Wi-Fi network. The LED shows two short blinks every second while the portal is open.
u177: Join the network named RECLINK-XXXX (the last two bytes of the board's address) on your phone or laptop. The factory password is reclinkfpv.
u178: Open http://10.0.0.1 in a browser. Your phone may warn that the network has no internet. Stay connected. RecLink does not force a login sheet, so you open the address yourself.
u179: Change the Wi-Fi password when asked (below). Up to three devices can be connected at once.
u181: While the password is still the factory default, the configurator shows this prompt each time you open it. Choose Yes, change it, type a new password of 8 to 31 characters and press Save & reboot. The board restarts and the Wi-Fi comes back with your new password. Tick Don't ask me anymore if you want to keep the default; the choice is stored on the board.
u183: If you forget the password you can still reach the portal by holding the button for 10 seconds to factory reset. That erases all settings and camera pairings.

u340: Stopping works the same way after a stop delay (default 1.5 s), so the last moments are not clipped.
u341: The camera is the judge: RecLink starts it, then waits for the camera to report it is recording. If it does not within the verify window, RecLink retries. u355: Zones: camera settings from a switch
u356: A 2–6 position switch or knob on your radio picks a zone. Each zone stores the camera settings you want, and RecLink sends them to the camera when the stick rests in that zone.
u370: Example settings for a GoPro. The zone applies once the stick has rested in it for the hold time (400 ms).
u371: A three-position switch split into three zones. The bar spans 900 to 2100 µs.
u373: GoPro: a zone does not load a GoPro preset. It pushes the settings you ticked (resolution, frame rate, lens and so on) to the camera's current video preset. DJI: each zone applies a camera Mode ID number instead, typed into a field on the zone row.
u377: Choose the AUX channel or press Set AUX and move the switch.
u378: Add or remove zones until the count matches your switch (3 for a 3-position switch). New edges are spread out by default: 1300 and 1700 µs for three zones.
u379: Move the stick through each position and check the bar's amber cursor lands in the right zone. Adjust the edges by dragging the handles. Edges stay in order and at least 25 µs apart. The last zone always ends at 2100 µs.
u380: Build the settings for each zone as shown on the next page.
u382: A zone must be held for 400 ms before it is applied, so a quick sweep through the middle does not fire every zone on the way. Change it under Advanced → Hold time before applying (50–5000 ms).
u384: Below the zone rows, one tab per zone shows a row for every setting a zone can change. Tick a row to push that setting; leave it unticked and the camera keeps its own value. Unticked rows are not stored.
u388: The lists follow the camera. With the camera connected and in a video preset, each option list shows only what it accepts right now (for example, only the frame rates valid at the current resolution). A value the camera no longer offers stays visible, marked "(not available now)".
u389: Order matters and is handled for you. RecLink writes resolution first, then the settings that depend on it, and Protune before its sub-settings. It waits for the camera to accept each write, checks the result, and retries a refused write once.
u390: Shutter is a shutter angle. 180° means an exposure of 1/(2 × frame rate). The zone keeps the same angle if you change the frame rate.
u391: Keep the camera in step while editing (on by default) means the camera really changes as you edit and as you select zone tabs. It works only while disarmed and not recording. Turn it off to edit without touching the camera.
u392: Models differ. Aspect ratio, Bit depth and Color profile are hidden for a HERO11 because it does not have them. A HERO12 or 13 shows them.
u396: Resolution, Aspect ratio, Frame rate, Lens, HyperSmooth, Bit depth, Color profile
u398: Protune on/off, ISO max, ISO min, Shutter angle, White balance, Color, Sharpness, EV comp, 10-bit
u400: RecLink applies a zone only when the camera link is ready, the camera is not busy, and it is not recording. To allow changes mid-recording, tick Allow zone changes while recording in the advanced options.
u401: If a blocker is in the way it retries on the next tick, without losing the choice.
u402: After a reconnect, the last selected zone is applied once, in case you changed the camera by hand.
u403: The Status tab's Zone settings row tells you the result: applied, partly applied (and which settings the camera refused), or not applied. The camera, not RecLink, decides what it accepts. Some options are not valid with the current resolution.
u404: A zone with no ticked settings pushes nothing.
u406: Zone 1 for cruising: 4K, 60 fps, Wide, HyperSmooth High. Zone 2 for a slow-motion pass: 2.7K, 120 fps, Linear. Zone 3 for max frame rate: 1080, 240 fps. Flip the switch in flight and the camera follows once the stick has rested for 400 ms.
u408: OSD: camera info in your goggles
u409: RecLink writes four lines of text, up to 16 characters each, into the four custom message elements you placed in chapter 4.
u419: Each line is a template: normal text plus % tokens that RecLink replaces with live values. The defaults are shown here. Anything the camera has not confirmed is replaced by nothing at all.
u420: Empty lines are sent as a single space so Betaflight does not show the placeholder name.
u424: Tap a line to select it (green border), then tap tokens in the palette to add them. Tap ＋ text to add literal text such as SD or BAT.
u425: Watch the preview. If a line would be longer than 16 characters the page warns "Line N is X chars, clipped to …". Shorten it.
u426: Prefer raw if you like typing templates directly, for example %st %et. Press Save settings.
u429: If the camera link is not ready, line 1 reads CAM LOST, or a blinking CAM ? while RecLink is still searching or connecting. Lines 2–4 go blank. This layout always shows, whatever your warning settings say, so the OSD is never silently stale.
u433: Digital keeps only glyphs DJI-style goggles draw: letters (uppercased), digits and basic punctuation. Battery bars become # and -. Analog leaves the text alone and allows the full character set, including a battery icon.
u435: 1–10 Hz. A change takes full effect after a reboot.
u438: Affects the %sp token only: km/h or mph.
u439: The token %wr shows the single most important active warning. A line with %wr in it makes the warning visible without a separate element.
u450: Record command not confirmed after all retries
u452: Camera battery at or below the threshold (default 15 %)
u454: Remaining recording time at or below the threshold (default 3 min)
u459: Blink warnings (default on) flashes the warning twice a second to catch your eye.
u460: Show a warning when the camera link is lost controls the warning shown by %wr. Line 1 still shows CAM LOST regardless.
u461: Set the battery and SD thresholds to taste on the OSD tab. Use 0 to disable one.

u464: Clock sync, GPS push and highlight tags
u465: Three smaller features that make your footage easier to sort and use.
u468: RecLink sets the camera's clock from the flight controller's GPS time, so every clip is stamped correctly, even after a battery swap that reset the camera to a default date. It writes to the camera only and never to the flight controller's clock.
u469: It syncs when all of these are true
u470: Clock sync is on, and (by default) the FC has a GPS with a steady 3D fix and at least 6 satellites for 10 seconds.
u471: The FC reports a plausible time.
u472: The camera is connected, not recording and not busy.
u474: When the camera connects, when the GPS fix becomes good, when you press Sync now, and then periodically (a GoPro every 5 minutes by default, a DJI every 60).
u475: For a GoPro it first reads the camera clock and only writes if it is more than 10 seconds off, then checks the result. A DJI cannot be read, so its time is simply sent.
u476: Set UTC offset in minutes (and Daylight saving) if you want footage in local time. Leave it at 0 for UTC.
u477: If the clock cannot be fixed after the retries, the OSD shows CLK FAIL and the Clock tab reports FAILED. Only the timestamp is affected.
u479: For a DJI camera only. On System → Send aircraft GPS position to the camera, RecLink streams the aircraft's GPS position to the Osmo at 1 or 2 Hz for the camera's own overlay or metadata. It needs a good GPS fix and valid time. A GoPro ignores this setting.
u482: A spare switch can drop a marker into the footage at a moment you want to find later. Choose its AUX channel (use Set AUX). When the channel rises above 1700 µs, RecLink sends a HiLight tag to a GoPro. A DJI has no highlight tag, so RecLink presses its Quick-Switch button instead.
u483: It works only while the camera link is ready. A momentary push-button is ideal.

u559: What you see in the air
u560: Wi-Fi is off. Only Bluetooth runs, so the camera link is as stable as it can be.
u561: The OSD text updates at its set rate. Recording state and elapsed time are always one glance away.
u563: Pressing the button in flight does nothing harmful.
u565: Camera link lost (out of range, camera off, radio dropout): OSD shows CAM LOST, the LED blinks fast, and RecLink keeps trying with growing pauses (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then every 30 seconds). When it reconnects it checks what the camera is doing and sends at most one corrective command.
u566: Flight controller link lost: RecLink stops writing text. The aircraft is unaffected.
u567: RecLink restarts (brown-out or stall): the OSD text freezes for about 0.3 seconds, then recovers. The camera reconnects by itself.
u573: wait 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, then 30 s, and scan again
u577: LED: idle blink / solid when recording
u580: The camera link lifecycle. SCAN, CONNECTING and SYNCING show as one searching state.
u583: Start with the LED and the Status tab. They tell you which of the two links, flight controller or camera, is the problem.
u584: Find the link that is down
u598: I cannot see the RECLINK network
u599: The portal only runs while disarmed and with the flight controller link up. Check the aircraft is disarmed and the LED shows two quick blinks per second. Hold the board's button for 3 seconds to open it by hand. It also closes after 15 minutes idle, so hold again if it went away.
u600: I joined, but the page will not load
u601: Type http://10.0.0.1 in the address bar. Stay connected even if the phone warns about no internet. Turn off mobile data if the phone keeps switching away. Up to three devices can connect at once.
u603: The factory password is reclinkfpv. If you changed it and lost it, hold the button for 10 seconds to factory reset. That also erases camera pairings.
u605: Press Save settings. Changes apply and persist only after saving. The bar says "unsaved changes" until you do.
u608: Check wiring: FC TX to RecLink RX and FC RX to RecLink TX. Check MSP is enabled on that UART at 115200. Try Swap TX/RX pins (advanced), save and reboot. If you changed the baud, match it on both sides.
u610: Confirm Betaflight is 2025.12 or newer, and that Custom message 1–4 are enabled and placed in the OSD tab. An OSD_UNSUPPORTED chip means the API is too old.
u612: The line is empty or RecLink is not connected yet. Check the FC link first.
u614: Match OSD type to your goggles. Digital filters to plain letters and digits. Use analog only for an analog OSD chip.
u616: Lines are limited to 16 characters. Shorten the template. The preview warns you.
u618: Check the 5 V supply. Add a 220 µF or larger capacitor across the board's power pads. Watch for WDT_RECOVERED or a rising reboot counter in Diagnostics.
u619: The camera is not found when pairing
u620: GoPro: put it in Connections → Connect Device → The Remote first, then press Scan now. Disconnect it from any phone app. Move RecLink closer. Make sure fewer than four cameras are already paired.
u622: Four cameras are the limit. Forget one on the Binding tab.
u623: REPAIR_NEEDED chip, or the camera never reconnects
u624: The camera forgot RecLink, usually after its connections were reset. Forget it on the Binding tab, then pair it again.
u625: It connects, then drops again and again
u626: Move the board away from carbon and battery leads. In Network (advanced) raise Bluetooth power to Max and reboot. After three silent hangs in two minutes RecLink reboots itself to clear the link.
u628: The camera is off, asleep, out of range or has dropped the link. Turn it on and wait; RecLink retries on its own.
u630: The camera has not confirmed them yet. Press Refresh camera state. Blank means unknown, on purpose.
u632: It does not record on arm
u633: Check Start / stop recording is set to a mode that includes arm, and the Status tab shows the aircraft as armed. Check the camera has a card and is connected (READY).
u635: The camera did not confirm recording. Check the SD card and that the camera is not busy. In advanced mode, raise Wait for camera to confirm or Retries. Open the Record trigger debug panel to see the last command.
u637: Use Set AUX again. Check the amber cursor on the bar moves when you flip it, and that the threshold sits between the off and on positions. For a push-button choose Trigger type: Button.
u638: Zones do not change the camera
u639: Check Enable zone control, the right AUX channel, and that the camera is in a video preset and not recording. Wait for the hold time (400 ms). Read the Zone settings row on Status.
u641: The camera refused those settings. Some options are not valid together, for example a frame rate with the chosen resolution. Pick values the lists offer, and use Capture from camera to start from a known-good combination.
u643: Clock sync needs a GPS fix with enough satellites and a camera that is idle and connected. See the Clock tab and press Sync now.
u645: With Advanced mode on, the System tab shows a short log and the Status tab shows counters and three debug panels. A screenshot of those, plus your firmware version from the header, is what you need when asking for help.

u693: What a single-colour LED does over a six-second window.
u694: Timings are nominal. On the production board the LED is a single-colour LED, so patterns differ by rhythm only. Boards with an addressable LED use colour too (blue for the portal, green for recording). The LED shows the highest-priority pattern that applies: portal, then a recent watchdog recovery, then recording, then flight controller down, then the camera link state. Identify overrides everything while it runs.

u844: RecLink links your flight controller to your action camera. The camera records when you arm, and its status appears on your OSD. This page takes you from the box to your first recording.
u846: Firmware 0.1.0 has been bench-tested only and is not flight tested. Do every step below with the propellers removed, and check that everything works before you fly.
u849: A flight controller with Betaflight 2025.12 or newer and a free UART
u850: A GoPro (HERO 11 or newer) or a DJI Osmo (Action 4, 5, 6 or 360), charged, with an SD card
u853: About 15 minutes, once. After that, RecLink starts by itself every time you power the quad.
u860: The camera keeps its own power
u861: Connect the four wires as drawn. TX goes to RX, and RX goes to TX.
u862: If the board resets by itself, add a 220 µF capacitor across its 5 V pads.
u863: Mount it near the camera, away from carbon fibre.
u864: Wires crossed by mistake? Fix it later in the configurator (Network → Swap TX/RX pins). No soldering.
u867: Open Betaflight Configurator and go to the Ports tab. On the UART you wired, switch MSP on. Leave the speed at 115200. Save.
u868: Go to the OSD tab. Tick Custom message 1, 2, 3 and 4 and drag them to a free spot on the screen. Save.
u869: On your radio, pick a spare switch for recording if you want one. This is optional.
u871: Betaflight must be 2025.12.0 or newer. Older versions cannot show RecLink's text.
u874: Power the quad (propellers off). Wait a few seconds. The RecLink LED blinks twice every second when its Wi-Fi is on.
u875: On your phone, join the Wi-Fi network RECLINK-XXXX. Password: reclinkfpv.
u876: Open http://10.0.0.1 in your browser. If the phone says there is no internet, stay connected.
u879: The Wi-Fi only runs while the aircraft is disarmed. Check that, or hold the board's button for 3 seconds to open it.
u881: After you change anything, press Save settings at the bottom of the page.
u884: In the configurator open Binding and press Pair GoPro.
u885: On the camera: swipe down, Preferences → Connections → Connect Device → The Remote.
u886: When the camera is pairing, press Scan now and tap your camera in the list.
u887: Press Pair DJI, then put the camera in pairing mode and accept the prompt on its screen.
u888: Pair once. After that RecLink reconnects by itself, and picks the strongest one if you have several (up to four).
u891: Nothing to change. By default the camera starts recording when you arm and stops when you disarm.
u892: To use a radio switch instead:
u893: Open Cam control. Under Start / stop recording choose From a radio switch.
u894: Press Set AUX, then flip your switch.
u896: Other choices: record on arm and the switch together, or only when both are on.
u899: RecLink writes four lines of text into the OSD elements you placed in step 2.
u906: Recording time left on the card
u909: You can change the lines on the OSD tab. Pick OSD type Digital for DJI-style goggles, Analog for an analog OSD.
u912: Propellers off. Run through this list before your first flight.
u915: The Wi-Fi appears. The OSD shows camera info, not CAM LOST.
u919: The Wi-Fi switches off. The camera starts recording.
u928: Wi-Fi is on, you can configure
u937: No link to the flight controller
u940: The LED blinks for 3 seconds, so you can find the board
u942: Turns the Wi-Fi on or off
u944: Factory reset. Erases settings and camera pairings. Not while armed
u948: Disarm the quad. Hold the button for 3 seconds.
u950: Type http://10.0.0.1. Stay on the Wi-Fi even without internet.
u952: Check Betaflight is 2025.12 or newer, MSP is on for that UART, and Custom message 1–4 are placed. Check the wires: TX to RX, RX to TX.
u954: Turn the camera on and wait. If it was never paired, do step 4.
u956: Put the camera in pairing mode first, then press Scan now. Disconnect it from other devices.
